title_en: Assassin's Creed Maker Ubisoft Confirms Further Layoffs, With 166 Jobs Lost From 2 Major Studios
summary_en: As gaming headlines focus on the launch of GTA 6, Assassin's Creed maker Ubisoft has announced another round of restructuring that eliminates 166 more jobs.
body_en:
Ubisoft has announced another round of restructuring that eliminates 166 more jobs.
In a surprising move, these positions are being lost from two of Ubisoft's most prominent studios: its enormous development hub in Montreal, which has led development on numerous Assassin's Creed and Far Cry blockbusters, and its sister studio in Quebec, which most recently launched last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows.
In a statement sent to IGN, Ubisoft blamed the job losses on an evolving portfolio and changing prodution needs, without specifying which franchises the impacted team members had been working on, or if any projects were no longer moving forward.
However, IGN understands that the layoffs affect employees whose projects have been cancelled or refocused, as well as those who could not be reassigned due to the decrease in the number of active projects.
"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," a Ubisoft spokesperson told IGN. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.
"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."
Ubisoft Montreal is currently deep in development on Assassin's Creed Hexe , the long-awaited new blockbuster entry in the historical stabathon series that's due to be set during the Witch Trials in Europe. Despite being announced years ago, there's still no word on when Hexe will actually launch. Earlier this year, the game lost its creative director Clint Hocking as part of a shake-up of leadership for the Assassin's Creed brand.
As for Ubisoft Quebec, while no further expansion plans for Assassin's Creed Shadows were announced for this year, fans were surprised to see its post-launch content curtailed so quickly compared to previous blockbusters. While Shadows sold well at launch, it's believed that the game failed to maintain this momentum, despite its feudal Japan setting being long-awaited by the franchise's community. As of now, it's unclear what else the studio is working on, or how today's changes will impact it in future.
